content.title: Start where everybody starts
content.text: ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Llama, Grok, Kimi, DeepSeek, Mistral. Different companies, different names, one kind of machine: a large language model, a program that reads text and predicts which text should come next. GPT is only OpenAI’s name for its family. The recipe is shared by all of them.

content.title: Zoom out: generative AI
content.text: Language models are one branch of generative AI: models that produce new content rather than only sorting or labelling what already exists. Their siblings produce images, video, voice and music. Same way of training, different kind of output.

content.title: Zoom out: deep learning
content.text: Generative AI is deep learning: networks with many layers, trained on very large data. Most of deep learning does not generate anything. It recognises faces, transcribes speech, ranks the next video in a feed, translates, plays Go, predicts protein shapes. Generating is the newest branch, not the biggest.

content.title: Zoom out: neural networks
content.text: Deep learning is a neural network with many layers. The network idea is older than the depth: the 1958 perceptron is one layer, and the networks of the 1990s had a few layers and read postcodes and cheques. “Deep” only means many layers stacked. It became practical around 2012, when data and graphics cards caught up.

content.title: Zoom out: machine learning
content.text: A neural network is one family inside machine learning: programs that adjust their own numbers from examples instead of following rules a person wrote. The other families do the same with different machinery: trees and forests, boosting such as XGBoost, regression, support vector machines, nearest neighbours, clustering. Several of them still beat networks on table-shaped data.

content.title: Zoom out: artificial intelligence
content.text: Machine learning is one branch of AI, the 1956 name for any program doing a task that seemed to need a mind. The other branches do not learn from data. Rules written by experts, search and planning like the chess computer that beat Kasparov in 1997, reasoning with probabilities, evolutionary algorithms, fuzzy logic inside washing machines and cameras. All of them earned money long before 2010.

content.title: Where today’s AI sits
content.text: Six layers, each inside the next. The AI everybody uses today is the innermost one: AI, machine learning, neural networks, deep learning, generative AI, and the language models at the centre. Every other branch is still there and still working. This series goes down to that centre, to the smallest piece that makes it learn.
